tool_args.rationale: The five pilots show monotone concavity over a narrow, single-gradient range, consistent with multiple candidate mechanisms. A low-cost open-branch probe can test whether behavior departs from the observed rising branch before committing to a fitted law.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a Haldane substrate-inhibition law now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The pilot only samples a rising, concave range; it does not identify whether the curve will turn down beyond the observed inputs.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a Cobb–Douglas power law now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The gradient is nearly constant across all five rows, so its exponent is not identifiable and the curve shape is confounded with other monotone-concave laws.
The target horizon is only 0.6 and the existing inputs already show a smooth curve; a branch-discriminating observation is more directly useful.
It is irrelevant to resolving the observed model-family ambiguity and has higher cost.
